thread:
sam/oncall: :rotating_light: noticing elevated queue lengths in us-west shortly after 13:02 UTC — requests piling up on hosted API. investigating.

maria/sre: seeing GPU util jump to 97% on pool-gpu-w1 around 13:02, admission controller started rejecting but backpressure propagated to edge proxies.

tyler/infra: 😬 logs show a sudden influx of long-context requests from a single customer namespace — many 8192-token calls.

olivia/runtime: can we confirm if prefix/KV caching was bypassed? those token counts would blow past expected sequences.

sam/oncall: digging. initial evidence: a client test with `max_tokens: 8192` and `stream: true` — they looped it via CI. traffic pattern looked like sawtooth bursts.

jordan/eng: deploy-bot posted this at 13:03: `deploy-checker: capacity-thresholds passed -> rolling target 0.9` — I think an autoscale decision coincided with the burst and caused a weird admission window.

deploy-bot: System note: `autoscaler` triggered scale-up attempt for pool-gpu-w1 at 13:04; provisioning delayed by 3m due to quota checks.

maria/sre: timeline summary so far: 13:02 burst -> 13:03 admission starts rejecting -> 13:04 autoscale requested but delayed -> 13:06 backpressure reached regional edge and routed to fallback models.

olivia/runtime: fallback routing routed requests to cpu-hosted distil model which then saturated its worker queues, causing retries and a small retry loop. we have traces:

```
2026-03-14T13:05:10Z request_id=abc123 route=/generate fallback_model=distil-1 queue_len=120 retry=1
2026-03-14T13:05:12Z request_id=abc124 route=/generate fallback_model=distil-1 queue_len=128 retry=2
```

tyler/infra: the admission controller used instantaneous `gpu_free_ratio` metric. the burst created a transient dip that made the controller clamp down too aggressively. Our smoothing/window was too short.

sam/oncall: impact: hosted API 5xxs for 8 minutes in us-west, increased latencies for other regions due to cross-region routing. customer-visible failures for ~2000 requests.

jordan/eng: cost note — fallback to distil spiked CPU costs since we had to spin up extra replicas under pressure. also wasted tokens from retries.

maria/sre: root cause (draft): rapid high-token burst from a customer test, combined with an admission controller that reacted to an instantaneous metric and an autoscaler that was blocked by quota checks, led to cascading fallback and retry amplification.

olivia/runtime: additional failure mode: KV/prefix cache had low hit-rate because the long contexts were unique per request, so batching didn't help and batching windows increased tail latency.

tyler/infra: config that made this worse:

```
admission_config:
  gpu_free_ratio_window_seconds: 5
  gpu_free_ratio_threshold: 0.12
  fallback_policy: route-on-reject
```

maria/sre: mitigation we applied in real-time: 13:08 increased `gpu_free_ratio_window_seconds` to 30s (temporary), tightened per-customer rate limit to 300 rps, and disabled immediate route-on-reject fallback for the affected pool.

sam/oncall: after mitigation, queue drained by 13:11, error rate back to baseline by 13:14.

jordan/eng: immediate action items (short):
- increase smoothing window for admission controller (30s -> 60s target) — tyler
- add quota preflight checks to autoscaler so it doesn't trigger partial/blocked scale-ups — tyler
- add per-customer long-context guardrail with explicit soft and hard limits — olivia
- adjust fallback policy to prefer queued spillover rather than immediate cross-model routing — maria

maria/sre: long-term items:
- telemetry: add a `reject-cascade` trace that correlates admission rejects -> fallback routes -> retry counts
- capacity planning: reserve short warm-up headroom for each GPU pool to handle sudden long-context bursts
- run chaos test simulating single-namespace token storm and validate autoscaler + admission behavior

olivia/runtime: PRs to open:
- infra#5234 add long-context guardrail hook
- runtime#1120 change fallback policy to `hold-and-backoff` for 60s before cross-routing

tyler/infra: I'll also add a safety that blocks autoscale if quota API returns a slow/5xx response — current behavior votes anyway.

sam/oncall: good notes. I'll draft a short postmortem and tag the SRE/infra/runtime owners. thanks everyone for fast triage :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident note saved: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/1863141592 — follow-up tasks assigned.

maria/sre: follow-up: please add the customer test-run logs to the issue so we can engage with the customer to prevent accidental CI storms.

jordan/eng: FYI cost estimate for the event: ~ $1.2k extra CPU/GPU burn. putting in finance ticket.

sam/oncall: closing thread; will post formal postmortem link when ready.
